turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
My predicted top five are **c030, c038, c044, c097, and c088**. I prioritize close, high-performing training analogues, then assess whether the changed interfaces and processing are likely to preserve their advantages. These are predictions—not measured efficiencies for the candidates.

### 1. c030 — Complementary electron extraction with a passivated PTAA interface
The closest training configuration is **ITO / PTAA | PMMA / MAPbI3 / PCBM-60 | Bphen / Al**, at **19.48%**. c030 retains that stack and adds IDTT2FPDI on the electron-extraction side.

PTAA provides hole selectivity without the acidic, hygroscopic PEDOT:PSS interface. A sufficiently thin PMMA layer can suppress interfacial recombination while permitting charge transfer. PCBM/Bphen supplies electron selectivity and separates the absorber from reactive Al. The additional acceptor could improve electron-side coverage or extraction, although its energetic alignment and thickness are not specified. The already-strong underlying recipe makes this my first choice.

### 2. c038 — Au-nanoparticle-modified NiO with an electron-contact interlayer
The training configuration **FTO / Au-np | NiO-c / MAPbI3 / PCBM-60 / Ag** achieves **20.0%**. c038 preserves that distinctive hole-contact stack, changes FTO to ITO, and adds PEI between PCBM and Ag.

Compact NiO provides electron blocking and hole extraction. The Au-nanoparticle modification has particularly strong empirical support here, potentially reflecting improved contact properties, absorber growth, or optical coupling. Thin PEI can modify the electron-contact dipole and reduce extraction losses. Its thickness is a significant uncertainty: excessive PEI would instead introduce resistance.

### 3. c044 — Strongly supported PTAA/PCBM/BCP/Cu combination
Two especially relevant training devices reach:

- **18.85%:** PTAA / PCBM-60 | C60 | BCP / Cu, spin-coated.
- **18.8%:** PTAA | PFN / PCBM-60 | BCP / Cu | Ag, spin-coated.

c044 uses the same core selective-contact combination, without those additional modifications. PCBM extracts electrons and can mitigate electron-side surface traps; BCP improves cathode selectivity and limits direct metal–absorber interaction. PTAA supports low hole-side recombination. This is a well-supported high-efficiency candidate, although removing the extra C60 layer may sacrifice some coverage or contact protection.

### 4. c097 — Close analogue of a high-performing complementary-acceptor stack
The sulfur analogue, **ITCPTC-Th | C60 | BCP with P3CT-Na and Ag**, reaches **18.49%**. c097 substitutes ITCPTC-Se while retaining everything else.

P3CT-Na offers a selective hole contact, while the complementary acceptor/C60 stack can improve electron extraction and interfacial coverage. Importantly, the training data favor the **C60/BCP version** over the corresponding ITCPTC-Th/Rhodamine 101/LiF recipe, which reaches **16.41%**. Selenium substitution could alter packing and energy levels, but I would not assume it necessarily improves performance.

### 5. c088 — Established PTAA/C60/BCP/Cu chemistry with a plausible coating process
Closely related PTAA/C60/BCP/Cu devices achieve **18.62%** with sequential spin coating and **19.085%** with slot-die coating. Doctor-bladed PTAA/C60/BCP with Ag also reaches **16.9%**.

Willow glass retains an ITO-coated glass electrode rather than introducing a fundamentally different contact. Doctor blading can produce continuous, high-quality absorber films, although drying and crystallization control remain important. Its strong contact-stack analogues place it narrowly within my top five.

**Final: c030, c038, c044, c097, c088**
